title: Money 3
note: B2 vocab leaf, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane. b1_money (36) owns the everyday layer — afford, waste, owe, debt, loan, instalment, mortgage, budget, expenses, payment, invoice, fee, savings, account, currency, invest, profit, bankrupt, property, luxury, wealthy, greedy, donate — and a1_shopping and a2_shopping own price, cost, cheap, expensive, cash, change, discount, refund, bargain, purchase. The corrected sweep also caught inheritance, taught this morning by leaf_family_b2 whose node is still `coming` — fifth self-collision this lane has avoided that way. What is left is the machinery an adult meets and cannot name: borrowing properly (overdraft, interest rate, lender, borrower, creditor, repay, repayment, collateral, credit rating), the paperwork of paying (direct debit, standing order, current account, transaction fee, exchange rate, tax return, deduction, allowance, expenditure, subsidy), and the language of getting by or not (cost of living, disposable income, make ends meet, well off, hard up, frugal, windfall, nest egg, splash out, rip-off, value for money, haggle) — that last board is the one that makes a B2 speaker sound like a person rather than a bank statement. C57 card 0 recaps Money 1 and 2. Build-the-family is half recap: borrow and lend are already the student's (taught in b2_false_friends, where the pair is the false-friend trap) and this unit adds borrower and lender; repay -> repayment and credit -> creditor run inside the unit. E10 Use is rewrite production.

cards.title: You already know
cards.note: Money 1 and 2 gave you the words for having and spending — money, price, cost, cheap, expensive, cash, change, discount, refund, afford, owe, debt, loan, budget, savings, account, invoice, fee, profit, wealthy. Those carry the sentences here. What is new is the machinery around them: how borrowing actually works, the paperwork of paying, and how people really talk about having enough or not.
cards.note_cz: Money 1 a 2 ti daly slova pro mít a utrácet — money, price, cost, cheap, expensive, cash, change, discount, refund, afford, owe, debt, loan, budget, savings, account, invoice, fee, profit, wealthy. Ta nesou zdejší věty. Nové je to okolo: jak půjčky doopravdy fungují, papírování kolem placení a jak lidé opravdu mluví o tom, jestli mají dost.
